answer.answer: AURORA addresses early multilingual misinformation detection, an area receiving less attention than English-only approaches. PROMID Task 3 consists of multilingual, highly imbalanced Russia–Ukraine conflict tweets collected during the war’s first year, manually annotated, with 8,388 merged training rows. AURORA classifies messages as misinformation or non-misinformation with a confidence score and supports real-time verification through an interactive dashboard. The paper reports significant generalizability and competitive performance on PROMID, but the supplied evidence provides no numerical metrics or detailed model architecture.

AURORA: Automated Understanding and Recognition of
Omnilingual Misinformation Artefacts
Kailasa Sai Charan1, Utkrisht Suman 1, Roshan Jain 1, Jasneet Kaur 1 and Shakshi Sharma1,∗
1School of Artificial Intelligence, Bennett University, Greater Noida, UP, India
Abstract
Misinformation has disseminated more quickly due to social media’s explosive growth, especially during politically
delicate or crisis-driven situations, such as the conflict between Russia and Ukraine. To lessen its detrimental effects
on society and assist policy makers, journalists, and social media moderators, early detection of false information is
crucial. In this study, we introduce AURORA, a generalizable, timely, and multilingual misinformation detection
system that categorizes social media messages as either misinformation or non-misinformation along with a
confidence score. The PROMID Task 3 dataset, which was made available at the 17th Forum for Information
Retrieval Evaluation (FIRE) 2025, is used to train our method. It includes multilingual, highly imbalanced tweets
about the conflict between Russia and Ukraine. We utilize several machine learning and transformer-based

3.1. Data acquisition & Wrangling
Data collection: We used the dataset provided by the FIRE Conference2 2025 Shared Track named
Prompt RecOvery For Misinformation Detection (PROMID) Task 3 i.e. Misinformation Detection in social
media texts. Precisely, this task aims to classify the tweets pertaining to Russia-Ukrainian War conflict
as misinformation or non-misinformation tweets. The dataset was collected using the official Twitter
API during the first year of the conflict and manually annotated by [19] following the framework [20].
This dataset contains multilingual words and highly imbalanced dataset that further make the problem
complex for generalization purposes.
Data Wrangling: Organizers provided two train data files i.e. misinformation & non-misinformation
tweets along with their labels & one test file for the final submission. We first merge these train set files
together containing total rows 8,388. Next, in order to make the data ready for model training in the

4. Conclusion
In this study, we presented a multilingual misinformation detection framework that can detect fake
content in a variety of languages and topics. Our approach showed significant generalizability when
tested on real-world fact-checking scenarios and achieved competitive performance on a highly imbal-
anced dataset provided by the PROMID Shared task at FIRE Conference, IIT, BHU in 2025. By providing
real-time verification capabilities and clear evaluation indicators, the interactive dashboard AURORA
further closes the gap between research and practical deployment. Despite the system’s encouraging
outcomes, there are still a number of directions for future research. First, multimodal settings like
images and metadata—which are increasingly employed in fake news campaigns—can be incorporated
into the model to improve it. Second, robustness could be further enhanced by resolving class imbalance
using sophisticated methods like contrastive learning or data augmentation. Lastly, incorporating large

etc. [8, 9, 10]. Researchers have also employed more advanced techniques including combining deep
learning and graph structure namely, Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) [11] and Knowledge Graphs [12].
One of the main goals of previous fake news studies has been the identification of false information
mainly in English language [13, 14, 15, 16] or separate models for each language [17]; multilingual has
received less attention [3, 18]. Moreover, early detection of false news is still a challenging task, thus,
we developed a model that can automatically detect any recent news article irrespective of the language
and topic.

based dashboard AURORA, where a user can ask on the fly any news being misinformation or not.
